candidates.source_name: Ephrem the Syrian / Commentary on Numbers
candidates.source_attribution: Ephrem the Syrian, Commentary on Numbers, on 10:1-10. NPNF Series 2, vol. 13. PD.
candidates.draft_body:
Ephrem the Syrian Commentary on Numbers (c. 365 AD)

On the silver trumpets sounded for war and for festivals (Num 10:9-10), Ephrem reads the doubled liturgical-and-military use of the trumpet as the canonical pattern: the same sign that summons the people to battle summons them to rejoicing — both belong to the Lord, both invoke remembrance before him. Tewahedo liturgical practice preserves the silver-trumpet tradition in the qabaro and silver-trumpet of the great feasts (Mäsqäl, Timqät); the same trumpet that announces the procession of the tabot announces the day of remembrance. Num 10:9 is the canonical anchor for the trumpet-as-prayer in Ethiopian worship.
